sections.html:
Deeds can be filed at either of two Iredell sites, in Statesville or Mooresville. The counters stay open Monday through Friday, eight to five.

  • Statesville site: 211 Constitution Ln, Statesville, NC 28677, telephone 704-872-7468
  • Mooresville site: 610 E Center Ave, Mooresville, NC 28115, telephone 704-663-4533
  • Shared fax line: 704-878-5426

Staff at these counters also issue certified birth and death certificates, marriage licenses and military discharge copies, and give notary oaths. Almost every record is open to anyone. Military discharges are the lone exception.

A seller typically never visits. The closing attorney carries in the signed deed along with the buyer's loan paperwork, and a later call to either site confirms both made the record and in what order.

sections.h2: Why recording matters in a sale
sections.html:
Until a deed is recorded, the transfer carries no weight with outsiders. Clerks index the deed and the lender's security instrument by party name, and the filing time decides who is first in line.

North Carolina's recording statute withholds a conveyance's force from lien creditors and paying buyers until it is registered in the county of the land, and then ranks claims by registration time. So a closing is not done at the signing table, and attorneys hold funds until recording is confirmed.

Drafting help and title opinions are off the menu for staff, as are title searches. Changing the names on a deed means a fresh one, drafted, notarized and recorded, which is why most owners hire a lawyer.

Judgments live with the Clerk of Court, 704-832-6600. One lasts ten years, may be renewed for ten more, and attaches to land you own now or acquire later. Have your attorney check for entries against you ahead of signing a sale contract.

For an ordinary instrument the fee is $26.00 through page fifteen and $4.00 per page beyond. A loan security document starts at $64.00 for thirty-five pages. Both follow G.S. 161-10, which applies in all one hundred counties alike.

No other charges stack on top of this schedule, and payment is due when you file.

Already-recorded documents are copied at county prices. Deeds are $.25 a page and a printed recorded map is $1.00, with an added charge for mail, so phone before sending a request.

sections.h2: Who pays the deed transfer tax?
sections.html:
Whoever transfers the property owes this tax, and the Register collects it before the deed is placed on record. The charge is $1.00 per $500 of price, rounding any leftover fraction up to a full $500.

The excise tax statute sends half the receipts to the Iredell general fund and the rest to the state revenue department.

It is figured on the price or value of the interest changing hands. Since the duty falls on the seller, find this line on your settlement statement and ask your attorney how the contract treats it. A cash offer does not change it, because the tax follows the deed, not the buyer.

A link on the county Register page opens a search of deeds, deeds of trust, plats and powers of attorney. Records stretch from December 1788 to today and are indexed by party name, as state law requires.

The Land Records page offers a search guide, indexing rules and a separate guide for property recorded before 1964. The online portal may show incomplete results during a software change and is not an official record, so for a sale request a certified copy from the office instead of printing from the screen.

  • Find an owner: use the tax office GIS maps, or call 704-878-3020 for help with them.
  • Proof a mortgage is paid: your lender files a certificate of satisfaction, and staff can mail or email you a copy.
  • Replace a lost deed: give names and a purchase year, and a copy costs $.25 per page.

A deed passes ownership, usually seller to buyer. A deed of trust is a three-way tie between borrower, lender and a neutral trustee that secures a loan. A lender's title policy protects the lender, while an owner's policy is optional and protects you against defects a title search missed. The office recommends carrying both.

sections.h2: Property tax and the Register of Deeds
sections.html:
You do not pay property tax at this office. Tax Administration in Statesville bills and collects it, while the Register only records instruments. The two meet at a sale, because a buyer's attorney expects the tax account to be current.

On request the collector will accept a payoff at the closing table, or a prepayment at last year's rate before the new bill is out. The county charges .50 per $100 for 2026, per its rates page, and towns like Statesville and Mooresville add their own.

January 1 fixes ownership for tax purposes. Close later in the year and the bill is still yours unless the contract shifts it, so check the proration line on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: A seller's steps at the Register's office
sections.html:
Take these steps so recording goes without a hitch.

  1. Engage a North Carolina attorney to draft the deed, because staff will not.
  2. Sign in front of a notary, and the attorney takes the notarized deed to Statesville or Mooresville.
  3. Pay the transfer tax and filing fee at the time of filing.
  4. Ask for word that the deed and any loan paperwork made the record, and note the filing order.
  5. Keep the lender's certificate of satisfaction for any loan you paid off.

To see what is on record before listing, search your name in the online index, then ask the office for a certified copy of anything that matters.

A few contacts help along the way. For parcel maps and finding an owner, call 704-878-3020. For judgments, call the Clerk of Court at 704-832-6600. For anything about recording, the Statesville site is 704-872-7468 and the Mooresville site is 704-663-4533. Keep the closing attorney in the loop on all of them, since the attorney controls when the deed is sent.

Mid-2025 population stood at 211,798, with roughly 93,711 housing units. Owners fill 71.9 percent of occupied units (2020-2024) and the typical owned house is $321,400. The midpoint household earns $81,419, rent at the midpoint is $1,252 monthly, and 1,835 building permits were issued in 2025.

faqs.q: Which office should I use to record a deed?
faqs.a: Either one. The Statesville site at 211 Constitution Ln and the Mooresville site at 610 E Center Ave both accept recordings on weekdays between eight and five.

faqs.q: What does it cost to file a deed in Iredell County?
faqs.a: A routine instrument is $26.00 up to fifteen pages, and every extra page adds $4.00. Deeds of trust start at $64.00 for thirty-five pages, then add the same $4.00 per extra page.

faqs.q: Who bears the excise tax on a sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays it before the deed is filed, at a dollar per $500 of value. Your contract and closing statement show how it is handled.

faqs.q: Can county staff prepare my deed?
faqs.a: No. State law bars them from drafting deeds. Hire a North Carolina attorney, then bring the signed, notarized deed in for filing.

faqs.q: Where do I check for a judgment against my property?
faqs.a: The Clerk of Court at 704-832-6600 holds them, and the Register does not. A judgment lasts ten years and may be extended for ten more.
